Avery / Ben — reviewed Clearwave's redlines. High level legal position and recommended counterpoints below. Attaching a clean counterproposal and an evidence checklist for triage.

Summary legal positions (recommended):
1) Defense v. Reimburse: We should resist unrestricted customer defense/control for all third-party IP claims. Defend-and-control materially increases Redwood's exposure (attorney selection, settlement authority, privileged communications).

2) Compromise approach: offer defend-and-control for narrow categories (e.g., literal copying of provided software or embeddings traced to customer data) and reimbursement with cooperation requirement for other types of alleged claims (e.g., claims alleging model-generated similarity).

3) Notice & evidence: require written notice within 30 days of Customer's receipt of claim (or as soon as reasonably practicable) and a defined evidence package (see attached evidence_checklist.xlsx). We should reserve the right to request additional evidence before assuming defense.

4) Subrogation & settlement: Redwood must retain settlement approval above threshold (e.g., amounts that create ongoing obligations) and be able to limit settlement that admits liability on Redwood's behalf. Any settlement that materially affects Customer rights requires Customer consent.

5) Carveouts for AI-generated output: propose a limited carveout — Redwood will not indemnify claims that are solely based on outputs generated by Customer prompts unless Customer supplied training data that induced infringement. This narrows exposure for model hallucinations.

6) Insurance / escrow: if we accept broader defense-control, require higher cap or a one-time credit / reduced price / increased insurance requirement.

Attachments: indemnity_counterproposal.docx, evidence_checklist.xlsx

Next steps:
- Ben: propose commercial offsets for the legal positions above (credit or cap trade).
- Avery: coordinate a 30-min call with Clearwave procurement; legal will take the call if needed.

Matt — thanks for the redlines. We've discussed internally and propose the compromise below to balance Clearwave's need for operational control and Redwood's need to manage legal exposure.

Proposed compromise (short):
- Defend-and-control: Redwood will accept defend-and-control only for claims that incontrovertibly arise from literal copying of Customer-supplied software/assets (Category A).
- Reimburse-and-cooperate: For claims alleging similarity/AI-generated output (Category B), Redwood will reimburse reasonable defense costs and will cooperate fully, and will have the right to request additional evidence under the timeline below before accepting defense.
- Notice & evidence: Customer to provide initial written notice promptly and provide the evidence checklist items within 30 days. Redwood may require supplemental technical evidence before assuming defense.
- Settlement authority: Redwood retains authority to settle claims up to $50k without Customer consent; settlements creating ongoing obligations require Customer approval.
- Commercial tradeoff: Redwood can offer a one-time credit equal to 6% of first-year ARR in exchange for accepting Category A defend-and-control.
